knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper establishes that systems of Hecke eigenvalues in the coherent cohomology of mod p abelian type Shimura varieties match those in their Hecke-equivariant subschemes. It extends previous results for zero-dimensional smooth subschemes to higher-dimensional and singular cases, including Ekedahl-Oort strata and central leaves. The proof utilizes a further going-down argument involving intersections with length strata to handle singularities and lack of nowhere vanishing sections.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper outlines its structure, with Section 2 providing notation and background on Shimura data and G-zips, and Section 3 proving the main theorems. It defines the special fiber of the Kisin-Vasiu integral model and establishes that the stack of G-zips is a smooth algebraic stack of dimension 0. For Hodge-type Shimura varieties, a smooth surjective morphism exists from the special fiber to the stack of G-zips, allowing the definition of automorphic vector bundles via pullback.

It establishes the concept of G(A_p^f)-equivariance (Hecke-stability) for sheaves and subschemes, noting that Ekedahl-Oort, length, Newton strata, and central leaves are equivariant. The unramified prime-to-p global Hecke algebra is defined, and the Hecke action on coherent sheaves is introduced via push-pull operators.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text proves that the maximal smooth open subscheme of a G(Ap f)-equivariant system of closed subschemes is itself equivariant. It establishes that powers of ideal sheaves, their quotients, and associated conormal sequences are G(Ap f)-equivariant. Additionally, it provides lemmas stating that nowhere vanishing sections on reduced schemes are injective and that symmetric powers of inclusions of locally free sheaves on regular schemes are injective.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text proves that for locally closed Hecke-equivariant subschemes of Shimura varieties, the systems of Hecke eigenvalues in their cohomology are equivalent to those of the ambient variety or specific strata. The results extend to noncompact cases and subschemes defined by nonvanishing loci of Hecke-equivariant sections.
